Situation1: A family member has a significant event they want to share with everyone.
Situation2: This is the last weekend before the partner relocates abroad for months.
Story:
I sat at the kitchen table, my phone buzzing with messages. My daughter had just called, her voice bubbling with excitement—my grandson had won his first art competition, and the whole family was gathering for a surprise celebration tonight. She wanted me there, said it would mean the world to him. I could already picture his proud little face, the way he’d look for me in the crowd.

But then, another message flashed on my screen. It was from Anna, my girlfriend. She reminded me, gently, that this was our last weekend together before her big move overseas. We’d planned a quiet evening, just the two of us, to savor every moment before the distance set in. She’d been counting on this, and so had I.

My heart twisted. I wanted to be the grandparent my family expected, present and supportive. But I also wanted to be the boyfriend Anna needed, cherishing our fleeting time. The weight of both roles pressed on me, each tugging in a different direction, and I sat there, torn, unsure which part of my heart to follow.
